copy.blurb:
Thursday 25 June 2026 at 20:00 UTC. Curaçao and Côte d'Ivoire on the card. On the Curaçao side, the engine's number sits +14.7pp clear of the market — a wide disagreement by the engine's standards this far out from kickoff.

Elo numbers going in: Curaçao 1790, Côte d'Ivoire 1740. That's a 50-point lead for Curaçao — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Curaçao to win at 42%, the draw at 27%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 31%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Curaçao to win at 27%, the draw at 28%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 63%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Curaçao side — 27% on the market, 42% on the engine, a +14.7pp gap.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Curaçao side that lower bound is 34% — +7.2pp clear of the market's 27%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 37 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Curaçao a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Curaçao are mispriced. Our number reads 42% on the home side; the market reads 27%. The +14.7pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Curaçao v Côte d'Ivoire · the model leans Curaçao
